LESSON: LABORATORY APPARATUS AND INSTRUMENTS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Scientific Investigation
Topic 1.3: Laboratory apparatus and instruments

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Laboratory apparatus and instruments. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are basic science skills important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the basic skills in science
2. use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory
3. use the SI units for basic and derived quantities in science
4. appreciate consumer protection when handling different apparatus, instruments, and other materials in day-to-day life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LABORATORY APPARATUS AND INSTRUMENTS
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Laboratory apparatus and instruments helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: LABORATORY APPARATUS AND INSTRUMENTS
Study Laboratory apparatus and instruments like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the basic skills in science

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the basic skills in science. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the basic skills in science.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Laboratory apparatus and instruments” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the basic skills in science. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory

What this means
In this part you learn to use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Laboratory apparatus and instruments matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use the SI units for basic and derived quantities in science

What this means
In this part you learn to use the SI units for basic and derived quantities in science. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the SI units for basic and derived quantities in science.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Laboratory apparatus and instruments this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the SI units for basic and derived quantities in science. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate consumer protection when handling different apparatus, instruments, and other materials in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate consumer protection when handling different apparatus, instruments, and other materials in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate consumer protection when handling different apparatus, instruments, and other materials in day-to-day life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Laboratory apparatus and instruments” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate consumer protection when handling different apparatus, instruments, and other materials in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Laboratory apparatus and instruments is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Laboratory apparatus and instruments” around your school. (skill: describe the basic skills in science)

Example 2: Say why Laboratory apparatus and instruments matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Laboratory apparatus and instruments this week. (skill: use the SI units for basic and derived quantities in science)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Laboratory apparatus and instruments” around your school. (skill: appreciate consumer protection when handling different apparatus, instruments, and other materials in day-to-day life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Laboratory apparatus and instruments to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the basic skills in science.
3. Practise this skill: use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.
4. Practise this skill: use the SI units for basic and derived quantities in science.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Laboratory apparatus and instruments from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Laboratory apparatus and instruments: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Laboratory apparatus and instruments?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are basic science skills important?
2. How are quantities in science expressed?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Laboratory apparatus and instruments means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the basic skills in science.
5. Be able to: use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
